answers.answer: Each player takes twelve ordinary turns. A courtship has no ordinary player turn, service rotation, Servants’ Hall use, or monument income; it resolves the courtship event only.
answers.evidence: Overview; Round-track events: courtship is only the courtship event.

answers.answer: Hosting order: rotate Quarters to Available, then Expended to Quarters (each one space); resolve the round event, then ongoing monument/Servants’ Hall effects; choose an activity tile; invite the exact required gentry; provide all required service; resolve positive favours before negative favours; optionally buy one Market or Reserve tile; cleanup by sending used servants to Expended, played gentry to personal discard, and returning the tile to its tableau column flipped/upgraded as required. Only the last player advances the marker after cleanup.

Pass order: all servants directly to Available; all gentry in discard to hand; resolve event then ongoing effects; choose £200 or a free Market refresh; optionally buy one tile; last player advances the marker. Servants used for ongoing effects are expended at turn end. Butler’s Room hiring is an activity, not a passing benefit.

Yes. Screening is fixed at the end of step 2, when reputation is 6.1, so the PR6 tile and guests qualify. Service Help can move one servant from Servants’ Quarters to Available Service for three reputation increments; it cannot take a servant directly from Expended. Later reputation loss to 3.4 does not change the screening level for this activity.
answers.evidence: Reputation, wealth and special actions: screening is fixed at end of step 2; Service Help row.

answers.answer: Resolve all positive favours before all negative favours; otherwise their order is your choice. You cannot take a negative reputation favour first to avoid its loss at minimum. A money penalty must be fully paid; use available positive money favours, a money VP card, or Borrow Money (£100 for two reputation increments), and if unable to fund it you cannot play that guest/tile.

Borrow Money: lose 2 reputation increments, gain £100, repeatable. Service Help: lose 3 increments and move one servant from Quarters to Available, repeatable; cannot take it directly from Expended. Refresh Market: lose 4 increments and fully refresh Market, once per turn. At minimum 1.1 you cannot take a special action. Service Help cannot take a servant straight from Expended.

Host the Butler’s Room activity with an available butler or underbutler and no gentry; take up to two Servants for Hire (not underbutlers), paying no money, into Expended Service. On first use the room upgrades. Its upgraded alternative recruits one common footman, valet, or lady’s maid from any location on one opponent’s family board into your Expended Service instead of taking up to two from supply; unique servants cannot be recruited.

A housekeeper may substitute for a lady’s maid only when no lady’s maids are available. With a Brushing Room in your tableau, footmen may substitute for valets only when no valets are available. An underbutler may substitute for any base male servant (butler, valet, footman) even if that servant type is available.

The only way to acquire an underbutler is to purchase Butler’s Pantry; take one from supply immediately into Expended Service. It is not immediately available: ordinary rotations move it Expended→Quarters, then Quarters→Available, reaching Available at the second subsequent rotation. Passing or Refresh Service can accelerate availability; once in Quarters, Service Help or the Servants’ Quarters tile can enable earlier use. Another player cannot recruit it.

Market price is the Market space price plus the tile’s printed modifier; Reserve base price is £300 plus the modifier. Price cannot be below £100. You cannot acquire a duplicate tile already owned, but reputation does not restrict purchasing a tile above your reputation.
answers.evidence: Builders’ Market and Reserve, first paragraph.

answers.answer: When a Market space empties, slide remaining tiles left and draw replacements into the rightmost spaces. A duplicate is stacked on its matching Market tile and another is drawn; duplicate tiles share one space and its price. Qualifying Reserve tiles go directly to Reserve and another is drawn. When filling multiple spaces, sort only newly drawn tiles by sorting number. Buying one tile from a two-tile stack leaves the space occupied, so no refill occurs.

After courtship 1, move all Market Service tiles except Largest Wine Cellar to Reserve; later Service draws also go there, with the same exception. After courtship 2, move all Market PR1 tiles to Reserve and send later PR1 draws there too. Largest Wine Cellar never enters Reserve. Full Market refresh after each of the first three courtships is standard, after Reserve movement.
answers.evidence: Builders’ Market and Reserve—Open Reserve and Refresh; Courtship and seasonal upkeep.

answers.answer: At each courtship first return both Fairchilds to Alderley Hall. For courtships 1–3, score the current face-up theme category, including negative tile VP; only the currently face-up hybrid category counts. Highest score gets one VP card and chooses one Fairchild for hand; each tied high player draws a VP card and no Fairchild is awarded. Everyone discards one secret objective; shuffle discards together and bottom-deck them. Then open Reserve, fully refresh Market, reveal the next theme to the right of previous themes, pass first-player marker anticlockwise, and advance the round marker.

Final courtship totals tile VP for all four revealed themes, with repeated categories counted repeatedly, including negative VP. Highest gets one VP card and a Fairchild; a tie is broken by highest reputation level (wheel position ignored). If still tied, no Fairchild is awarded and tied players draw VP cards. Discard the final objective, then players get a final chance to use special actions and VP-card benefits where possible; move the marker to Wedding Bells and score.

End-game VP: face-up improvement tile VP (including negative/unused); gentry VP in hand and discard (including family and final Fairchild, excluding dismissed guests); fulfilled remaining objectives; reputation by levels 1–7: 1/3/6/10/15/21/28; 2 VP per servant of any type/location; 1 VP per £200, rounded down; and printed VP on retained unused VP cards. Tie sequence: final Fairchild holder wins; otherwise highest reputation level wins; if still tied, share victory. Wheel position has no effect.

Normally get five objectives at setup and two at round 6, discard one at each of four courtships, leaving three to score. Additional objectives from Main Library or an Objective VP card add to retained total and do not cause an extra discard. Simultaneous discards are shuffled together face down and put on the deck bottom. Tile objectives require owning named tiles at game end; they need not be upgraded.

A VP card may be used immediately when drawn, at any time on your later turn (multiple cards allowed), and once more after final courtship before scoring. Reveal and discard a used card to the bottom of the VP deck. Retained unused cards stay hidden with objectives and score their printed VP; you cannot take both benefit and final VP.

A normal activity tile must flip to its rose/upgrade side after first use; an already-upgraded normal tile stays on that side. Ongoing-only tiles cannot host or upgrade. Hybrids start with underlined category showing, flip after every use, and move to the newly face-up category. A tile that upgrades into a monument can host once, upgrades, and never hosts again; monument effect starts on later turns. Only the currently face-up hybrid category counts at courtship and for objectives.

Monuments pay one reputation per ordinary turn during ongoing effects on hosting or passing, but not courtship; a newly purchased monument first pays on a later turn. Servants’ Hall works during ongoing effects on hosting or passing: place one available servant there to reduce one opponent’s reputation by one and gain one yourself; that servant cannot also serve the activity and goes to Expended at turn end. Do not target a player at minimum reputation.
answers.evidence: Improvements and ongoing effects—Monuments; Servants’ Hall.

answers.answer: Heritage Guest Suite: one footman on tile, one casual guest from hand with normal service; doubles all guest favours, including negative; upgrades and remains an activity. Queen’s Suite: housekeeper on tile, one prestige guest from hand with normal service; doubles one chosen favour; upgrades into a monument. Lionheart Suite: butler on tile, draw one prestige guest from deck to attend, no personal guest service; doubles nonnegative favours, not negative ones; keep guest and discard it at cleanup; upgrades into a monument. Each suite has a fixed one-guest count that cannot be changed.
answers.evidence: Improvements and ongoing effects, Suite activity table and following paragraph.

answers.answer: Choose a random first player. Starting with the player to that player’s left and going clockwise, players choose available base family boards. Asquith adds the Dowager Countess as a fifth family card; Cavendish starts at reputation 1.4; Ponsonby gains £300; York adds a footman to Available Service.

Each player starts reputation level 1, position 1, using stacked 1/2, 3/4, 5/6 and Max counters with 1 showing (no 7/8 counters). Starting servants in Available Service: one butler, housekeeper, valet, lady’s maid and footman. Starting tiles: Private Study, Butler’s Room, Main Gazebo, Front Parlour and Bowling Green, starter/building icon showing. Family cards: Lord, Lady, Heir and Young Lady. Only Ponsonby starts with money (£300); Asquith/Cavendish/York bonuses are as stated in Q21.

For three players, Servants for Hire gets 3 valets, 3 lady’s maids, 6 footmen, and 2 underbutlers total. No butlers or housekeepers are placed there. Unused servants returned to the box are unavailable for the game and cannot later be hired.

Separate starter guests from casual deck, shuffle starters, and deal two to each player; shuffle every unused starter back into the casual deck. Starter guests are casual guests with a starter icon and otherwise follow normal casual rules; they are not a separate guest type during play.
answers.evidence: Setup step 4; Gentry, screening, dismissal and family.

answers.answer: For four players, select one double-sided monument per player plus one, so five monuments go in the bag. Choose at most one of Sculpture Garden and Garden Maze. Tiles that later upgrade into monuments always go in the bag and do not count against the setup selection.

Fill six different eligible Market spaces with tiles of PR3 or less (including no PR), excluding Servants’ Hall and double-sided monuments. Set ineligible draws aside and return them to the bag after filling. Stack duplicate eligible draws in a matching space. Normal tiles start with upgrade/rose icon hidden; hybrids with underlined hybrid icon showing. Sort the six spaces by ascending sorting number beginning at £300 space. PR4 tiles, Servants’ Hall and double-sided monuments are ineligible.

Put Alderley Hall standard side up, round marker at 1, one reminder token per player above track; shuffle theme and VP decks separately; reveal first theme face up (open courtship), keeping themes in order; put base Charles and Elizabeth Fairchild face up on Alderley Hall. The first theme is not hidden and old themes stay revealed when new ones are revealed.
answers.evidence: Setup step 9; Courtship and seasonal upkeep.

answers.answer: At hosting rotation, the servant in Quarters moves to Available; the servant in Expended moves to Quarters. Each advances one space and Expended servants are not moved twice. An unused Available servant remains Available.

No. The round event resolves before activity selection, and a Private Study not already upgraded at that step gives no reward; hosting it later does not retroactively grant the Fair reward. An already-upgraded Study gives £300 and 2 reputation on Village Fair spaces 3 and 9 only.
answers.evidence: Round-track events, Village Fair; Private Study.

answers.answer: On space 6, Draw Objectives resolves during the round-track event before ongoing effects and before activity selection on hosting, or after returns and before ongoing effects on a pass. Draw two and keep both secret with your objectives. Passing players receive it too, since all round-track events use the same timing for host and pass.
Yes. On National Holiday space 14, ignore PR on all tiles and guests when hosting. All other requirements still apply, including service and exact gentry counts/types.

Yes. During Builders’ Holiday (or Market Purchase VP benefit), buy any number from Market and/or Reserve within funds. Complete purchases from the unchanged market at prices that applied before the sequence; no sliding/refilling between purchases and no refresh between purchases. Refill resulting empty Market spaces together after the sequence. Market Purchase VP-card use follows these same rules.
answers.evidence: Round-track events; Builders’ Holiday / Market Purchase VP card.

answers.answer: Set all Market tiles aside, leave Reserve unchanged, refill all six spaces from bag under normal refill rules, then return the set-aside tiles to bag and mix; they cannot reappear during that same refresh. Reserve tiles remain untouched.

Each reputation symbol is one increment. Moving past position 5 to 1 raises a level; past 1 to 5 lowers a level. Standard minimum is 1.1 and maximum is 7.5 (Max.5); losses below minimum are ignored. To avoid wasting gains at Max.5, spend excess immediately on special actions, including before or during a reputation favour to create space.
Money is public. Players may not give or receive money from one another. You may never spend more than you hold. The supply is unlimited; use proxies if needed.

For a two-ladies requirement, female family members or female guests may fill it. For two casual guests, only casual guests count; family cannot. You must play the exact number/types, with no extra gentry. Family cards need no personal service or reputation threshold; family members have no PR.

An ordinary nonscreening guest invite draws one card from the indicated deck, reveals it to everyone, and adds it to hand (unless a larger explicit draw count applies). A screening invite draws the stated number, reveals only the kept cards, and adds those to hand; rejected cards go unseen to the bottom of their guest deck.
answers.evidence: Gentry, screening, dismissal and family—invite rules.

answers.answer: Dismissal is optional, so you need not dismiss if you have no unwanted guests. You may dismiss a guest from hand, current activity, or discard, including one just drawn by an earlier favour. Family cannot be dismissed. Put dismissed guest on bottom of matching deck; it ceases to be yours, is not returned on passing, and scores no VP.

Lord: £200. Lady: choose either screen two casual guests and keep one, or optionally dismiss one guest. Heir: choose £100 or one reputation. Asquith Dowager: both £100 and one reputation. Lady and Heir offer choices; Lord and Dowager provide their listed benefit(s), with Dowager receiving both.

The Young Lady gains the admirer bonus only when a male prestige guest attends the same activity; it is two reputation. A male casual guest and a female prestige guest do not qualify. Charles Fairchild is male and prestige, so he qualifies. She still draws one casual guest in all cases.
answers.evidence: Base family card table; Fairchild gender/type paragraph.

answers.answer: Charles is male, prestige, no PR, requires a valet, and gives three reputation. Elizabeth is female, prestige, no PR, requires a lady’s maid, and gives both one prestige guest and two reputation. They are guests, not family cards, and may be dismissed under the normal guest-dismissal rule.
answers.evidence: Gentry paragraph; Charles Fairchild gives three reputation; Elizabeth gives both…

answers.answer: Miss Elizabeth Perkins reduces one opponent’s reputation by one. Miss Florence Oliver reduces one opponent by two and costs you one reputation. Minimum-reputation protection applies, so a player at 1.1 cannot be targeted by a reputation-reducing opponent effect.
answers.evidence: Base gossip cards paragraph; minimum-reputation rule.

answers.answer: A Barn gives one reputation whenever you host an Estate activity. It gives nothing merely for owning an Estate tile and nothing when passing.

Ordinary rotation moves all Quarters servants to Available and Expended servants to Quarters, one space each, at hosting-turn start. The Servants’ Quarters improvement instead permits directly using one servant still in Quarters after rotation, in addition to Available Service; no reputation cost. That servant goes to Expended at turn end. Service Help costs three reputation increments to move one Quarters servant to Available, and cannot take directly from Expended.
answers.evidence: Servants’ Quarters tile; Service mechanism table.

answers.answer: Front Private Study requires a butler and two family, with no tile favour. It upgrades permanently into an ongoing tile after use. Once upgraded, it pays £300 and two reputation only on Village Fair spaces 3 and 9; it cannot be hosted repeatedly to gain that income.

Unupgraded Main Library uses a butler and two family and draws one extra objective. Upgraded Main Library uses a butler and three family and draws one VP card. Extra objectives increase retained objectives for final scoring and do not trigger extra courtship discards.
answers.evidence: Main Library; Objectives and VP cards.

answers.answer: The Objective VP benefit draws two objectives, keeps one, and puts the other on the bottom of the objective deck. It adds one retained objective and does not cause an extra discard, so final objective count increases by one.
answers.evidence: VP-card benefit table; Objectives and VP cards.

answers.answer: Yes. Refresh Service moves all servants directly to Available, including Expended servants, usable immediately. Service Help costs three reputation increments per servant and moves only one servant from Quarters to Available, never directly from Expended.

Hire Servant takes one servant from Servants for Hire (not underbutler) into Expended Service. It cannot immediately provide service from there unless another rule refreshes it; ordinary rotation moves it first to Quarters and then to Available on the next rotation.
answers.evidence: VP-card benefit table—Hire Servant; ordinary rotation table.

answers.answer: Yes. Refresh Guest may return any one gentry, including a family member, from your personal discard to hand. If returned before Invite Gentry, you may select it to attend this activity if it meets normal requirements; returning it does not itself play it.

The basic-servant objective counts only common footmen, valets, and lady’s maids, excluding butler, housekeeper, and underbutler. Ordinary service scoring gives 2 VP for every servant of all types and locations. The ten-servant objective gives 7 VP for at least ten servants total.

Both upgraded Queen’s Suite and Lionheart Suite count for the monument objective (3 VP per monument). Category objectives count a hybrid only in its currently face-up category; Queen’s/Lionheart are monuments.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference; Improvements and ongoing effects—Hybrids.

answers.answer: Nature Group is 11 VP for Flower Room plus one garden: English Garden, French Garden, Sculpture Garden, or Garden Maze. Domestic Group is 12 VP for Gabled Conservatory plus either Main Library or North Library. The tiles need only be owned at game end; they need not have been used or upgraded.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference; group objectives paragraph.

answers.answer: The prestige-guest objective scores 1 VP per prestige guest; the every-three-guests objective scores 1 VP per complete group of three nonfamily guests. A final Fairchild counts as a prestige guest and nonfamily guest. Incomplete groups score nothing.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference; objective definition paragraph.

answers.answer: The reputation objective earns 7 VP for reaching maximum level 7, regardless of wheel position. The wealth objective earns 10 VP for at least £1200. Ordinary reputation VP depends on level only (1/3/6/10/15/21/28 VP for levels 1–7), not wheel position; reputation ties are also by level, not wheel position.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference; Final VP and tiebreak paragraph.

answers.answer: Both sides of base West Terrace require one butler and exactly three family. Unupgraded favour: draw one prestige guest. Upgraded favours: draw one prestige guest and optionally dismiss one to four guests from hand, current activity, or discard to the bottom of their matching decks. It remains an activity on both sides and never becomes an ongoing dismissal tile.
answers.evidence: Improvements and ongoing effects, West Terrace paragraph.

answers.answer: There is no hand or personal discard-pile limit. Gentry in discard still belong to you and score normally; passing returns them to hand.

You may inspect all Reserve tiles at any time and buy any one, including a tile underneath another in a stack; there is no top-tile-only rule. Every Reserve tile is public and available for selection.

No, you are not required to host whenever possible; you may choose to pass. If a preferred activity lacks required gentry or service, choose another legal activity or pass; if no activity is possible, you must pass.

Yes. A passing player can take the free pass refresh, use one paid special-action refresh (four reputation increments, once per turn), and use multiple Market Refresh VP cards in the same turn. The once-per-turn limit applies only to the paid special-action Refresh Market, not the passing refresh or VP-card refreshes. During a Builders’ Holiday or Market Purchase buying sequence, however, no refresh by special action or VP card is allowed between purchases.
answers.evidence: Reputation, wealth and special actions; Builders’ Holiday / Market Purchase VP card.
